official_sources.title: Scottish Government: Circular 1/2024, householder permitted development

permitted_development: Scotland uses Class 1A for single-storey ground-floor extensions and Class 1B for ground-floor extensions with more than one storey.

depth_rules.title: Extension projection and boundaries
depth_rules.intro: Scotland uses Class 1A for single-storey ground-floor extensions and Class 1B for ground-floor extensions with more than one storey.
rules: For Class 1A, on or within 1m of a boundary, rear projection is limited to 3m for a terrace and 4m for other houses, measured from the relevant rear wall.
Class 1B does not permit any part of a multi-storey extension within 10m of a curtilage boundary.

height_rules.title: Other limits and restrictions
rules: Class 1A limits overall height to 4m and eaves to 3m. Class 1B cannot exceed the existing house height.
Check footprint and front/rear curtilage coverage limits, road-facing elevations and all remaining conditions.
These extension rights do not apply in conservation areas, to flats or to houses created under Class 18B or 22A; listed building consent may also be required.
